front.title: BGP Service-Route distribution in AI data centers

abstract.t:
AI clusters and hyperscale data centers can contain hundreds of leaf switches and large numbers of service prefixes. In a conventional BGP leaf-spine design, each spine distributes routes for the service prefixes originated by one leaf to all other leaves. This leads to a large number of received BGP route instances on the leaves and many FIB entries for service prefixes on the spines.
This document describes an alternative deployment in which dedicated eBGP speakers, referred to in this document as Service RRs, distribute service routes. The spines continue to distribute infrastructure routes but do not carry service routes. A Service RR uses regular eBGP procedures while advertising service routes with NEXT_HOP unchanged. The leaves encapsulate the service traffic and the spines forward the encapsulated service traffic using infrastructure reachability.
The design improves control- and data-plane scaling by reducing the number of service-route instances received by each leaf and removing service-route state and processing from the spines. This document defines no new BGP extension.
